feedback: Approved to race unchanged. Iteration 0 is the only raced evidence: the baseline (base_speed 1.6, kp 2.0, kd 0.3, sensors at x = ±0.04) left the track on all 60 development trials (20 per track), with max_error about 0.062 m against the 0.06 m off-track limit, about one line-loss event per run, and progress of 0.49 (oval), 0.22 (s-bend) and 0.11 (slalom). This candidate responds to that evidence in four ways: base_speed lowered to 1.3, kp lowered to 1.6, kd raised to 0.5, and sensor span widened to ±0.06 m. Each change addresses a specific failure, and the set is valid within the contract limits (sensor x within ±0.08, weights within ±2, line_loss an allowed option). The speed and damping changes are a sensible first step because the baseline failed on bends rather than stalling. The 3.0 s limit may not be met at 1.3, but completion is worth far more than time, so staying on track comes first. Nothing here is obviously broken, and the race is needed to show whether the changes help. After the race, read the telemetry as follows. If max_error stays above 0.06 m or runs still end off track, lower base_speed further (toward 1.1) before changing the gains. If the robot stays on track but progress is short or completion_time is above 3.0 s, raise base_speed in steps of about 0.1 while watching max_error. If line_loss_events remain above zero on the sharpest bends, test line_loss at search_left or search_right, matching the side the robot leaves the line.
requested_changes: If the race shows off-track ends or max_error above 0.06 m, lower controller.base_speed from 1.3 toward 1.1 first, since the baseline's speed of 1.6 left the track on every trial.

If the robot stays on track but completion_time is above 3.0 s or progress is short, raise controller.base_speed in steps of about 0.1 while watching max_error, and keep kp at 1.6 unless steering_oscillation rises.
If line_loss_events stay above zero on the tightest bends after the sensor widening to ±0.06 m, test controller.line_loss at search_left or search_right, matching the side the robot leaves the line.
